reviewer: Astra independent scientific and engineering review

coordinator_reported_independent_scoring.population: two fabricated stable/unstable events, no KIKI trajectories

engineering_evidence.validation_attribution: Fixture results were supplied by the coordinating agent; this review inspected test and runtime source and independently verified bindings and budget arithmetic. No duplicate numerical execution was performed.

review_notes: Both candidates share the frozen A06 seed324 step240 mass, sine-edge shape, damping shape, deterministic local-port amplitude and time-scale initialization. The model has 22 fitted shared coefficients; the T1 event correction is inferred from the causal history, not stored as a fitted event parameter.

The A06 origin was restricted to original source train. This new scope reads that checkpoint once and does not import its encoder, event latent states, normalization or optimizer. Runtime checks anchor mass against frozen TASK3 static mass.

History and target scales use the complete train roster only. The registered speed RMS floor is 1e-5 rad/s. The fixed memory radius is three times the square root of mass-weighted train historical velocity mean square; the topology radius is 0.6. Only initial hidden states are projected; subsequent propagation uses the passive equations.

Five Gauss-Newton updates use the fixed 1e-6 penalty on absolute normalized proposed latent states. The augmented least-squares construction matches the stated mean-residual objective. Its singular values describe regularized numerical conditioning, not observational identifiability.

Full-train gradient accumulation, 72-update cap, 0.006 Adam learning rate, gradient norm cap 1 and shared stiffness/damping bounds [0.5,2] match the protocol. Checkpoints are evaluated on the full 107-case val at updates 0,12,24,36,48,60,72, with the registered common plateau stop and no retries.

Inside the fixed TASK3 six-term trajectory gate of 0.5, selection first minimizes unresolved/uncovered/numerically invalid cases, then allocated minus TP minus TN, then trajectory score and earliest update. Outside the gate, finite trajectory score ranks first. This preserves complete-roster error denominators and cannot silently count unresolved cases as stable.

The scientific call budget was independently recomputed from 864 complete training batches, 14 full val checks, final complete train/val scoring for both candidates and one eventwise isolation pass after each failed evaluation batch. It exactly matches all registered operation limits.

The reader permits only train then val in this stage. Initial pair and preprocessing are saved before val access. Final selected pair and preprocessing are hashed before formal train/val evaluation. Test data are inaccessible to this fit stage and require a separate exact frozen-artifact authorization.

Final scoring preserves both numerical steps, all cases, failures and unresolved results. The target of full test accuracy above 90 percent means 76 resolved cases and at least 69 correct cases; it is not a promise of outcome or an independent-data claim.
limitations: The minimal bridge retains memory energy and augmented-solver diagnostics, but does not preserve event topology coordinates or raw unregularized observability spectra. This round supports paired prediction comparison, not real topology recovery or identifiability claims.
Synthetic transfer validates the registered structural family and the new fixtures validate the regularized interface. Neither establishes that the real TASK3 data follow that family.

This receipt approves the exact scientific implementation and finite fit scope. Runtime policy activation, explicit registered stage approval, clean committed checkout and required integration checks remain enforced before scientific execution.
